newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's JSE wary of too rapid black empowerment.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's JSE wary of too rapid black empowerment.

text.p: The executive president of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) warned on Wednesday that there were dangers in carrying out the process of black empowerment too quickly.
Russell Loubser told a news conference for the release of the JSE's 1996 annual report that black economic empowerment was a vital process, but should not happen at an unsustainably quick pace.
"There is a danger of things just exploding completely out of control...if something is going to become very big, very soon, do you have the management expertise to manage it?" he said.
The growth of black influence on the JSE has been speedy, spearheaded by shift to black control at industrial holding company Johnnic and at mining house JCI.
In 1992 there were only five black-run companies on the JSE with a market capitalisation of 1.8 billion rand. In 1996 the figure was 17 firms worth 26.5 billion rand.
But Loubser praised the high quality of black entreprenuers breaking into South Africa's once white-ruled business world and said it was vital the process continued.
"It is totally imperative that it has to grow and it has to grow every year," he said.
